en.title: Minimum Maximum Adjacent Gap After Deleting k Numbers
en.description:
Keep n−k of the original elements, sort the kept elements, and take their maximum adjacent difference; minimize that value. When only 1 element is kept, this site's convention is that the maximum adjacent difference is 0. The source text is truncated; the objective of this problem was recovered from its complete example explanation, and it is not to minimize the maximum minus the minimum of the whole range.

The standard I/O, examples and solution were written independently by this site; ranges marked as this site's are not the original source constraints.
en.input: The first line contains n k, and the second line contains n numbers. The original snapshot gives no value bounds; this site sets 1≤n≤200000, 0≤k<n, and values in −10^9..10^9.
en.explanation: Example 1: keep 3, 4, 5, for a maximum adjacent difference of 1. Example 2: only one element is kept, so the answer is 0. Example 3: no number can be deleted, the adjacent differences are 3, 4, 1, so the answer is 4.
hints: After sorting, only n−k consecutive elements need to be considered; on the array of adjacent differences, maintain the maximum of each window of length n−k−1, then take the minimum.
